attack_mechanism: For a ordinary execution instruction, `exec_done` is produced by the default `(e_state == E_EXEC)` completion arm. `openMSP430.e_state` sets the selected completion class, execution state, or transition into the required terminal state; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`. An attacker who forces `openMSP430.e_state` away from its terminal value can keep the selected predicate false on successive `mclk` cycles. The operative RTL path is `openMSP430.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. Decode and fetch remain blocked waiting for completion, creating a persistent loss of instruction retirement.

For a jump-completion instruction, `exec_done` is produced by `exec_jmp ? (e_state == E_JUMP)`. `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_branch` sets the selected completion class, execution state, or transition into the required terminal state; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`. An attacker who forces `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_branch` away from its terminal value can keep the selected predicate false on successive `mclk` cycles. The operative RTL path is `openMSP430.frontend_0.inst_branch -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. Decode and fetch remain blocked waiting for completion, creating a persistent loss of instruction retirement.
